label: Route
description: An HTTP endpoint: each call to its path (and method) starts a fresh run carrying the request. The fixed ports carry method, path, query and headers, and the body comes out whole on `body`. Declare the body's type to have it checked before the run starts (`-> (body: Signup)` with `type Signup = { email: String, age?: Number }`, `..` before the closing brace to drop keys it does not name): a body that does not fit is answered 400 naming the field, and nothing downstream runs. A field declared as a file kind (`photo: Image`) takes a `data:` URL or base64 and receives the stored file. A port you add on the arrow reads the path capture of its name (`-> (id: String)` on `cards/{id}`). Answer with Reply, Stream or Close downstream.

inputs.name: path
inputs.label: Path
inputs.description: Path under the project's live URL: literal segments and `{name}` captures (`users/{id}`), or empty for the root address. No leading '/'. Two routes may overlap only when one is strictly more specific (`cards/count` beside `cards/{id}`); otherwise activation refuses the pair.

inputs.name: method
inputs.label: Method
inputs.description: HTTP method served. Empty serves every method; another method on a served path gets 405.

inputs.name: dataType
inputs.label: Body shape
inputs.description: Body shape. `json`: the body is JSON on `body`, held to the type declared there (a record type or `JsonDict` takes one object, `Json` any JSON value); one that does not fit is answered 400. `text`: the whole body is a String on `body` (declare `-> (body: String)`). `bytes`: the body is stored and its stored-file value lands on `body` (declare `File`, or `Image`, which is checked against the bytes). Reply and Stream answer in this shape unless their `answerAs` says otherwise.

inputs.name: auth
inputs.description: Auth access node (ApiKeyAuth, HmacAuth, or one of your own). Unwired, anyone with the URL may call. The established identity comes out on `caller`.

inputs.name: maxSessionSecs
inputs.label: Give up on one connection after this long
inputs.description: Hard ceiling on one connection, no default: it cuts a healthy feed on the clock. Only for an `outlivesCaller` run that has nothing else ending it (TagRun/StopTagged is usually better).

inputs.name: callerSilenceSecs
inputs.label: Call the caller gone after this much silence
inputs.description: Seconds the caller's machine may leave sent data unacknowledged before the caller counts as gone. Bounds silence, not call length: a present caller acks automatically, so hours-long feeds are untouched. Raise for clients whose link sleeps. `0` uses the OS default (about fifteen minutes).

inputs.name: maxInboundMb
inputs.label: Largest request body, in MB
inputs.description: Largest request body in MB; bigger is answered 413. A `data:` URL inflates its bytes by about a third, so the default 16 fits roughly 12 MB of picture.

inputs.name: whenChunkFails
inputs.label: When a message cannot be sent
inputs.description: What happens when a Stream cannot turn one message into the route's `dataType` (a value that is not a String on a `text` route, a file it cannot read). `surface` (default): the Stream fails and the caller is told, with an error status if nothing was sent yet, the format's error marker after. `drop_chunk`: that message is skipped, noted on the run's record, and the stream goes on; pick it when one missing message is fine, like a frame of a live feed. A run that fails, or a bus that ends failed, is told to the caller either way.

inputs.name: whenCallerIsSlow
inputs.label: When the caller reads slower than you send
inputs.description: What gives when a streamed answer is written faster than the caller reads it and the 256 chunks waiting for it fill up. `block` (default): the next write waits for room, so a slow caller slows the program and gets every chunk. `drop_oldest`: the oldest waiting chunk is thrown away, so the caller always gets the latest; pick it for live video or a price feed. `drop_newest`: the new chunk is thrown away and what was already waiting goes out in order. A dropped chunk never reaches the caller, so keep `block` for anything the caller must read whole.

outputs.name: fired
outputs.description: Always true on a call; gate work on "the route was called".

outputs.name: method
outputs.description: The HTTP method the caller used.

outputs.name: path
outputs.description: Path as called, no leading slash (`users/42`).

outputs.name: caller
outputs.description: What the auth gate established: JWT claims, `{"key": <index>}` for an API key, `{}` for HMAC. Null with no `auth`.

outputs.name: body
outputs.description: The request body, held to the type declared here: a record, `JsonDict` or `Json` for `json`, `String` for `text`, a file kind for `bytes`. A body that does not fit is answered 400 naming the field. Closed when the request carries no body (a GET).

then.message: Route '{id}' takes a json body: declare `body` as a record type or `JsonDict` for one JSON object, or `Json` for any JSON value, or set `dataType` to the shape the body has.
Route '{id}' takes a text body, which arrives as one String: declare `-> (body: String)`.
Route '{id}' takes a bytes body, which is stored as a file: declare `-> (body: File)`, or the kind it has to be (`Image`), which is checked against the bytes.
Route '{id}' path starts with '/'. The gateway prefixes the route automatically; drop the leading slash.

Route '{id}' starts a run that never answers its caller: no node that answers it (a Reply, a Stream, a Close) is in it. Wire the answering node so the run reaches it (through data, or `_should_flow` on the node or on the group it sits in).

Route '{id}' would exist once per instance, because {perInstanceReason}, but its public address is one for every instance. Keep the route shared and pick the instance per call: the `Weft-Instance` header on a route gated by a connection, or an instance token.
